subject: Science
title: Year 7 Science: Half-term 4 (Acids, alkalis and chemical reactions)

questions.question: Which pH is neutral?
questions.explanation: pH 7 is neutral, e.g. pure water.

questions.question: Universal indicator turns purple. What does this show?
questions.explanation: Purple means pH 12–14: a strong alkali. Red means a strong acid.

questions.question: Which of these is an acid found in the stomach?
questions.explanation: The stomach makes hydrochloric acid to help digest food and kill bacteria.

questions.question: A farmer adds lime (an alkali) to a field. Why?
options: To make the soil more acidic
questions.explanation: Lime raises the pH of acidic soil so crops grow better.

questions.question: What is the word equation for neutralisation?
What gas is made when an acid reacts with a metal like magnesium?
questions.explanation: Metal + acid → salt + hydrogen. Hydrogen gives a squeaky pop with a lit splint.

questions.question: What gas is made when an acid reacts with a carbonate?
questions.explanation: Acid + carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide (turns limewater cloudy).

questions.question: Which of these is a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Burning makes new substances (ash, carbon dioxide) and cannot easily be reversed.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a sign of a chemical reaction?
options: A change of shape when squashed
questions.answer: A change of shape when squashed
questions.explanation: Squashing changes shape but makes no new substance.

questions.question: What does a fuel need to burn, as well as heat?
questions.explanation: The fire triangle: fuel, heat and oxygen.

questions.question: What does this hazard symbol warn about: a liquid dripping onto a hand and a surface?
questions.explanation: That symbol means corrosive: it can burn skin and damage surfaces.

questions.question: What is the difference between a dilute and a concentrated acid?
options: How much acid is dissolved in the same volume of water
questions.answer: How much acid is dissolved in the same volume of water
questions.explanation: A concentrated solution has more acid particles in the same volume.
